evidence.finding: rabbitmq-server 3.5.7-1ubuntu0.16.04.4 and its erlang-* dependency chain (odbc, snmp, os-mon, ssh, tools, etc.) finished installing successfully on node3 without an apt kill/retry.

apt-get install -y -qq rabbitmq-server on node2 was still running (root apt-get + apt-get + _apt http method processes alive) after roughly 8+ minutes with no dpkg output for rabbitmq-server, i.e. it appeared stalled or extremely slow.
Executor killed the stuck apt-get with 'pkill -9 apt-get' and 'pkill -9 -f /usr/lib/apt/methods', then ran dpkg --configure -a, and started a second install (install2.log).

evidence.source: node2 install2.log polling 01:48–01:55 (three more sleep/poll commands)
evidence.finding: The retried install also ran for roughly 8+ minutes with apt-get and the _apt http method process still alive; dpkg -l did not yet show rabbitmq-server.
ss -tlnp on both node2 and node3 shows RabbitMQ ports (4369, 5672, 25672) listening — RabbitMQ eventually came up on both nodes.
rabbitmqadmin was fetched from the local management plugin and both Python 2.7.12 and 3.5.2 were present.
rabbitmqadmin declare queue against vhost 'payments' as user app_payments returned 'Access refused: /api/queues/payments/orders' (HTTP 403-equivalent).

pika was not installed; python3-pip was missing; an attempt to apt-get install python3-pip timed out at the 120s MCP proxy read-timeout window (the underlying apt-get process was still running and later completed on its own).

pip3 install of the latest pika (1.4.4) succeeded, but importing it raised 'SyntaxError: invalid syntax' on the line using a Python 3.6+ variable-annotation (`self._blocked_connection_timeout: Optional[float] = None`) — incompatible with the system Python 3.5.2 on Ubuntu 16.04.
Downgrading to pika==1.1.0 installed cleanly and imported successfully (version 1.1.0 confirmed).

A pika-based publish script ran successfully, printing 'publish_confirmed None' — publish succeeded but the confirm result value was None rather than an explicit True, which is unusual for a delivery-confirm publish and unverified/unexplained in the available evidence.

rabbitmqctl list_queues on vhost payments showed queue 'orders' with durable=true and slave_pids/synchronised_slave_pids listing rabbit@node3 and rabbit@node2 — i.e., the durable queue was mirrored to two nodes at that point.

Only 31 of 150 total command records were included in this redacted trace (up to 20 recent failures + 12 recent successes); 119 records, including whatever vhost/user/permission setup happened earlier, were omitted. No records show the actual `payments` vhost creation, app_payments user creation, or `set_permissions` calls.
Attempt terminated by executor_timed_out after 2100 seconds; no record in the provided trace shows a node being stopped/killed nor a consume-after-node-loss check being performed.

likely_causes.cause: Package installation for rabbitmq-server (and its large erlang-* dependency set) via apt-get on this Ubuntu 16.04 image was very slow and/or intermittently stalled, consuming on the order of 15-20+ minutes of wall-clock time across node2 alone (initial hang + kill + retry), which is a large fraction of the 2100s budget.

The default/latest pika client version is incompatible with the system Python 3.5 interpreter shipped on this Ubuntu 16.04 image, causing an import-time SyntaxError; this was only discovered after installing python3-pip and pika from scratch, adding further delay.

'Access refused' from rabbitmqadmin/management API for the app_payments user on the payments vhost indicates the account was missing vhost permissions (or the vhost/user/permission setup had a mistake) at the time management-API access was attempted; not enough evidence in the trace to confirm the exact misconfiguration since the setup commands are outside the redacted window.

The combination of the above delays (apt stalls, python/pika version mismatch, pivoting from rabbitmqadmin to raw pika scripts) consumed most of the time budget, so the task likely ran out of time before it could kill a node and verify the durable queue was still consumable from the survivors — the required end-to-end resilience test was not observed to have run.

next_attempt_guidance: Kick off `apt-get update` and `apt-get install -y rabbitmq-server` on all three nodes in parallel/background immediately at the start, and poll less frequently with longer intervals (or a single longer background job) rather than issuing repeated 60-120s sleep+poll commands that eat wall-clock time without acting; if a node's apt-get shows no progress for ~3-4 minutes, kill and retry once, not repeatedly.

Pin pika to a version known to work with the system Python (3.5.x on Ubuntu 16.04) up front — use `pip3 install 'pika==1.1.0'` directly instead of installing the latest version first and discovering the incompatibility.

Before relying on rabbitmqadmin/management HTTP API, explicitly create the `payments` vhost and grant the app account full permissions with `rabbitmqctl add_vhost payments` and `rabbitmqctl set_permissions -p payments <user> '.*' '.*' '.*'`, and confirm with `rabbitmqctl list_permissions -p payments` before attempting to declare queues via the API — this avoids the 'Access refused' detour.
Consider skipping the management-API/rabbitmqadmin path entirely for validation and using rabbitmqctl + a pinned pika client from the start, since that is what ultimately worked here.

Reserve explicit time in the run for the actual resilience test: after the queue is confirmed mirrored (durable=true with slave_pids on the other nodes), stop rabbitmq-server (or the whole node) on the master node, then verify the queue and message are still present and consumable from a surviving node before declaring success — this step was not evidenced as completed in the timed-out attempt.

Given apt/package installation was the single largest time sink observed, consider pre-warming or caching the rabbitmq-server package/dependencies if the image or environment allows it, or budget significantly more of the time allowance to installation before starting configuration steps.
summary: The attempt timed out after 2100s without evidence of completing the required resilience test. Observed facts: RabbitMQ installation via apt-get was slow and stalled on node2, requiring a kill and reinstall (each install phase took 8+ minutes); on node1, python3-pip was missing and had to be installed, then the latest pika (1.4.4) failed to import due to a Python 3.5 syntax incompatibility, requiring a downgrade to pika==1.1.0; an earlier attempt to use rabbitmqadmin against the payments vhost returned 'Access refused' for the app account, causing a pivot to raw pika scripts. By the last recorded action, a durable queue 'orders' had been created and mirrored to two nodes and a message had been published, but no evidence in the trace shows a node being killed or consumption from survivors being verified — likely because time ran out. The redacted trace omits 119 of 150 commands, including the vhost/user/permission setup, so the root cause of the 'Access refused' error cannot be confirmed from available evidence.
